name: Re-RAW At War

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline; its own on-air narration frames it as Re-RAW's first show under new owner Rebel Yell.

appearances.note: Led Lucifer Magnusson to the ring on a leash before his debut.
Attacked backstage by Orin LeBlanc before the main event, forcing Rum Barton into a handicap match.
Returned to Re-RAW after the main event, made the save for Rum Barton, and challenged Demola and LeBlanc to a tag match the following week.
Introduced to the crowd on Re-RAW's opening night; his own ring entrance was drowned out by the crowd.

matches.note: Re-RAW's opening match, a try-out for the two younger wrestlers; Read tapped to a Savaje Cobra Stretch before his own partner could tag in.

matches.stipulation: Originally a handicap match for Gregorson
matches.note: Magnusson, Gregorson's secret tag partner, made his Re-RAW debut mid-match; the two put Beauty and Iron through a table before Magnusson pinned Iron with a running spear.
Piper blasted F-Dot with a chair, then put Hussein on top of him for the pin once the referee recovered.

matches.stipulation: Handicap match (Barton's scheduled partner Jay Ruby was attacked backstage beforehand)
matches.note: Barton submitted to LeBlanc's Beast's Burden. LeBlanc then continued to beat Barton with a chair after the bell until a returning Doug McCray ran in for the save, hit Demola with the Devil's Deal, and announced a tag match the following week: himself and Barton against Demola and LeBlanc.

notes: Re-RAW's opening broadcast, posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy in two parts the same day; each part is served as its own page under this wing's archive. The broadcast's own retrospective video declares the predecessor promotion, RAW, dead, immediately followed by the on-screen text 'Re-RAW LIVES!' -- the primary-source basis for reading this wing as RAW Wrestling Federation's own 2005 relaunch.

name: Re-RAW At War #2

date.source: The broadcast's own dateline, live from Viking Hall, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

appearances.note: At ringside for Hostile Takeover's match against the Drunken Phone Call.
Attacked Drew Piper's own tag partner Ricky Hussein backstage after being paid by Piper to do so.
Announced the Pick It RAW fan-voted championship tournament and confirmed the main event's finish.

matches.note: Joined already in progress; Harper submitted Paul with a California Deathlock. Debut for both Harper and Lawson.
Won by disqualification after Hussein chaired Beauty to break up a pin.
Fenriz superpowerbombed Rheaume through a table from the ring apron; Mauler finished MAZHAT with his own Rope-a-Dope finisher for the pin.
Black Creek Bart pinned Krumm with the Black Creek Buster after Savaje powerbombed him.

No winner declared on air: Gregorson powerbombed both members of the Drunken Phone Call through a glass table at once, drawing a disqualification the referee never formally announced before Sexual Assault (Arron Iron and Ric Beauty) ran in with chairs for the save.

LeBlanc pinned McCray with a chair-assisted Snowblind on what owner Rebel Yell himself called a fast count; McCray then attacked Rebel Yell with the Devil's Deal. Yell let the result stand but booked LeBlanc against McCray one-on-one for two weeks later.

notes: Posted to rec.sport.pro-wrestling.fantasy in three parts the same day; each part is served as its own page under this wing's archive. Announces the Pick It RAW fan-voted championship tournament (leading into a pay-per-view, Rebirth, not in the held record) and unveils the new Re-RAW World Heavyweight Championship belt.

name: Re-RAW In Retrospect #3

appearances.note: Threatened Arron Iron and Ric Beauty ahead of a six-man match, in an interview segment at his own home.
Interviewed Werewolf Gregorson at his home, arriving a day late for the appointment.
Announced Casey Cool's arrival to Werewolf Gregorson.
Shown backstage the previous week having his wounds stitched by his wife and valet, Leah Maynard-McCray, and needled about a returning opponent, Drew Piper.
Stitched Doug McCray's wounds backstage and argued with him about his own in-ring decisions and his upcoming opponents.
Confirmed, in a studio interview, that he paid Terrell Griffin to attack his own tag partner Ricky Hussein.
Appeared in studio alongside Drew Piper and taunted Ricky Hussein over the beating he gave him.

notes: A studio recap-and-preview episode, not a card: gives the Pick It RAW tournament standings, an interview segment, and a preview of the following week's matches. No card or result of its own survives; the previewed matches are not in the held record and are not structured.
